sonnet.q1: The fallback: the daily popular-items list (20 item IDs), marked as a fallback. (Lookup limit is 30 ms; no features or timeout goes to step 4.)
sonnet.q2: The store keeps its last copy and the API keeps serving those features for up to 6 hours (feature check: no older than 6 hours). After that they count as missing and requests go to the fallback. Which timestamp the 6 hours counts from is an open question.
sonnet.q3: No, shadow output is never shown to a user. Shadow work is queued without waiting, and no user response waits on it, so shadow failures do not affect the user's response.
sonnet.q4: Users in the shadow group: 10% of users, picked by a fixed function of the user ID (so always in or always out), and only while the shadow alias is set.
sonnet.q5: The latest daily summary must show at least 7 days in shadow, error rate under 0.5%, p99 inference latency under 80 ms, and the ML lead must have approved the switch. If any fails, the alias is not moved.
sonnet.q6: Not decided. Product has not decided whether a live A/B test comes between shadow and the full switch; the plan leaves it open.
sonnet.q7: Each instance checks the active alias every 30 seconds. When it has moved, the instance loads the new version and reads its needed features, keeping the old version until loading finishes (and keeping it with an error log if loading fails). No redeploy; only the registry pointer moves.
sonnet.q8: A shadow worker reads the user's features from the online feature store itself. Shadow does not add latency because the API only puts a job on the shadow queue without waiting, and workers run the shadow model separately.
sonnet.q9: If the queue cannot take a job, the API logs that and carries on, and the job is dropped. NOT STATED for what happens when workers merely fall behind but the queue still accepts jobs.
sonnet.q10: Both are written to the prediction log (shadow output with inference time or skipped/error rows, and the 20 served items written by the API for shadow-group users). A daily comparison job compares per user the candidate's 20 IDs with the served 20 and writes a daily summary with days in shadow, error rate, p99 inference latency and list overlap.
sonnet.q11: The feature check before a model runs: every feature the model needs must be present for this user and no older than 6 hours. If not, the request goes to the fallback and the model never runs on features the store does not have. Each instance reads which features a version needs when loading it. For shadow, a failed check writes a skipped row and runs no model.
sonnet.q12: An operator moves the active alias back to previous, and the version rolled back from becomes previous. Instances check the alias every 30 seconds and then load the version, so it takes effect in about 30 seconds plus loading time, meeting the 1-minute limit as long as loading takes under 30 seconds.
